_note: SL-T suggestion heuristic for the risk tool, now driven by a two-axis risk model (likelihood x impact) as in the IEC 62443-3-2:2020 detailed cyber security risk assessment. HOUSE HEURISTIC: the standard prescribes no matrix; this mapping is a SolutionsPT house default. Every table below is a transparent SolutionsPT default, NOT reproduced from the standard. The tool always shows the rule trace; the consultant always sets the final SL-T (per foundational requirement) with a written justification. Where the client has their own corporate risk matrix, it takes precedence (hardRules).

slDefinitions._note: HOUSE summary of the four security levels, in SolutionsPT's own words, as the assessment uses them. Not the standard's text.
slDefinitions.1: Mistakes and chance misuse, with no intent to cause harm.
slDefinitions.2: A deliberate attacker with general IT skills, simple tools and little time or money.
slDefinitions.3: A deliberate attacker who knows control systems, using purpose-built tools and a moderate budget.
slDefinitions.4: A deliberate attacker who knows control systems in depth and has the backing of a large organisation, such as a state.

severityScale.name: Negligible
severityScale.note: No meaningful safety, environmental, operational, financial or regulatory effect.

severityScale.name: Minor
severityScale.note: First aid only, a short outage, a small cost or a minor reportable event, recoverable within a shift.

severityScale.name: Serious
severityScale.note: Injury, reportable release, multi-shift outage, material cost, or regulatory action.

severityScale.name: Severe
severityScale.note: Loss of life, a major release, loss of an essential function, or catastrophic cost or regulatory exposure.

likelihoodScale.name: Low
likelihoodScale.note: House default: no known history; would require an unlikely combination of access, capability and intent.

likelihoodScale.name: Medium
likelihoodScale.note: House default: plausible given the exposure and a capable adversary; occurrence would not be surprising over the system's life.

likelihoodScale.name: High
likelihoodScale.note: House default: known-exploited path, an exposed access point, or an actively targeted asset; expected without intervention.

riskMatrix._note: HOUSE risk matrix (unmitigated/residual risk = impact severity x likelihood). NOT the 62443-3-2 example matrix. Bands: low, medium, high, very-high. Tune per engagement or replace wholesale with the client's corporate matrix.

riskToSL._note: HOUSE mapping from an unmitigated per-FR risk band to a suggested SL-T for that foundational requirement. The standard prescribes no matrix; this mapping is a SolutionsPT house default.

low.trace: Unmitigated risk low: casual-violation protection (SL1) is a reasonable target for this foundational requirement.

medium.trace: Unmitigated risk medium: protect against intentional violation with simple means (SL2).

high.trace: Unmitigated risk high: protect against a capable, resourced, IACS-aware attacker (SL3).

very-high.trace: Unmitigated risk very high: SL3 as the working target; SL4 only where a nation-state-grade adversary is genuinely in scope (flag for a conscious decision rather than defaulting).

tolerableRisk._note: The organisation's tolerable risk is the highest unmitigated risk band accepted WITHOUT additional countermeasures. Any FR/threat whose unmitigated risk exceeds it must be treated. Default here is a placeholder; capture the client's real threshold.

exposureModifiers.label: Permanent or routine remote access (vendor or staff)
exposureModifiers.trace: Standing remote access materially raises the likelihood of an authentication/use-control/data-flow compromise.

exposureModifiers.label: Internet-reachable or connected to internet-facing zones
exposureModifiers.trace: Internet adjacency exposes the zone to opportunistic and targeted attack.

exposureModifiers.label: Wireless links into or within the zone
exposureModifiers.trace: Wireless extends the boundary beyond physical control.

exposureModifiers.label: Routine removable media use
exposureModifiers.trace: Removable media is a proven ingress route that bypasses network countermeasures.

exposureModifiers.label: Many conduits to less-trusted zones
exposureModifiers.trace: Each conduit to a less-trusted zone is an attack path to broker or reduce.

specialRules.label: Zone contains SIS / safety instrumented function
specialRules._floorFR: The foundational requirements the safety floor applies to. HOUSE default: all seven. A project can narrow it (project.safetyFloorFR), never widen it.
actions: Prompt: safety systems normally warrant their own zone, separated from basic process control.
Apply an SL3 floor to every foundational requirement for any zone containing a safety function.
Mark zone safetyRelated: true (carried into the interchange export).
specialRules.trace: Compromise of a safety function is a direct physical-harm path; common practice treats SL3 as the working floor and separation as the default architecture.

specialRules.label: Assumed adversary class exceeds suggested SL
actions: If the consultant's threat context assumes an attacker class above a suggested per-FR SL, flag the mismatch rather than silently raising.
specialRules.trace: The SL should resist the adversary you actually expect; a mismatch needs a conscious decision, not an automatic bump.

hardRules: Suggestion never exceeds SL4 and never silently changes after consultant override.
The rule trace (which rules fired and why) is always shown alongside the suggestion.
The consultant sets the final SL-T per foundational requirement; a justification is mandatory and is the primary deliverable text.
Unmitigated risk is impact x likelihood, rated before any countermeasure is considered; a threat whose risk exceeds tolerable risk needs a recorded treatment decision and is never silently accepted.
Where the client organisation has its own risk matrix/criteria, those take precedence over this heuristic; record that the client matrix was used.
